definitions.gloss: mixed tenancy; mixed-use occupancy; cohabitation of diverse tenants
definitions.explanation: A situation where different types of businesses, shops, or residents share the same building or area. Most commonly seen in the term {雑居|ざっきょ}ビル (mixed-use building).

examples.japanese: {雑居|ざっきょ}ビルの{三階|さんかい}に{事務所|じむしょ}がある。
examples.english: The office is on the third floor of a mixed-use building.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}には{雑居|ざっきょ}ビルが{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Mixed-use buildings line the area in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{雑居|ざっきょ}ビルは{防火|ぼうか}{対策|たいさく}が{不十分|ふじゅうぶん}な{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: Old mixed-use buildings sometimes have inadequate fire prevention measures.

notes:
USAGE:
{雑居|ざっきょ} most commonly appears in the compound {雑居|ざっきょ}ビル, referring to a building housing a miscellaneous mix of small businesses — bars, restaurants, clinics, offices, and other establishments all in one building. These are very common in Japanese cities, especially near train stations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雑居|ざっきょ}ビル (mixed-use building — the most common usage)
- {雑居|ざっきょ}{地区|ちく} (mixed-use district)
- {雑居|ざっきょ}{房|ぼう} (shared prison cell)

CHARACTERISTICS:
{雑居|ざっきょ}ビル typically have narrow stairways, many small tenants on each floor, and often host nightlife establishments. They are a distinctive feature of Japanese urban landscapes.
